references.text: Jeremiah describes God's word as a fire in his heart: "Then it was in my heart like a burning fire, shut up in my bones" (Jer 20:9). Jesus came to cast fire on the earth, and God's word is linked to the purifying and consuming power of fire.

Malachi prophesies about the Lord's messenger who will come as a refiner's fire and cleanse the sons of Levi (Mal 3:2-3). The coming of Jesus brings judgment and cleansing, as suggested by the fire in Luke 12:49.

John the Baptist proclaimed that the one coming after him would baptize with the Holy Spirit and fire, and that he had his winnowing fork in hand to clean out his threshing floor (Matt 3:11-12). This links the fire both to the coming of the Spirit and to judgment.

Jesus says in Matt 10:34-36 that he has not come to bring peace, but a sword, and that he has come to set a person against their father. This parallels Luke 12:49 where Jesus' coming brings division and conflict, as further described in Luke 12:51-53.

John's words that Jesus will baptize with the Holy Spirit and fire (Luke 3:16-17) are a direct parallel. The fire Jesus came to cast on the earth is linked to the fire of the Holy Spirit and the fire of judgment.

The following verses (Luke 12:51-53) elaborate on what the fire means: Jesus has not come to bring peace, but division. The metaphor of fire in verse 49 is explained through the division the gospel creates within families and relationships.

On Pentecost, tongues as of fire appeared, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit (Acts 2:2-4). This can be seen as a fulfillment of Jesus' desire to cast fire on the earth – the fire of the Holy Spirit that was poured out upon the disciples.
"For our God is a consuming fire" (Heb 12:29). God's nature as a consuming fire sheds light on Jesus' words about bringing fire to the earth – it is God's holy presence that purifies and judges.
